name: Entain
editorial_article: Entain is a seminal electronic album by the Finnish artist Vladislav Delay (Sasu Ripatti), originally released in 2000 on the influential German label Mille Plateaux. Often cited as a cornerstone of the glitch, microsound, and experimental ambient scenes of the early 2000s, Entain represents a pivotal moment in the development of modern digital music production. The album is characterized by its intricate, stuttering textures, complex rhythmic loops, and a profound, immersive atmosphere that challenges traditional notions of song structure.\n\nSonically, Entain leans heavily into the digital artifact—the sound of corrupted files, skips, and processor errors—transformed into a deeply emotive and coherent musical language. Ripatti’s approach here avoids the cold, clinical feel often associated with glitch, favoring instead a layered, organic-sounding synthesis that feels almost tactile. By weaving tiny sonic fragments into vast, evolving tapestries, the album captures a sense of suspended time, creating what fans have described as a space "beyond time and space." It remains a highly respected work for its pioneering use of digital manipulation, influencing a generation of producers interested in the intersection of organic emotion and digital failure. The 2023 remaster has helped reintroduce this atmospheric masterpiece to a new audience, solidifying its place in the experimental canon.
editorial_pitch: A seminal work of early 2000s glitch and experimental ambient, Vladislav Delay’s 'Entain' is a masterclass in weaving complex digital artifacts into deeply immersive, rhythmic textures.
